thread:
jamal: Rolling a lightweight rust-gpu-exporter to 50% of GPU nodes tonight. Lower memory and faster startup, but it exports per-process metrics by default — we need a sampling plan before we flood TSDB :grimacing: https://git.internal/rust-gpu-exporter

alex: what's the default sampling? full pid list every scrape? that'll explode series count

mira: default is full per-pid. On busy nodes that becomes thousands of series (containers+pids+cmdline). Proposal: top-k sampling + label whitelist + drop cmdline

jamal: Canary flags we validated on a small pool:

```
--pid-sampling=topk:5
--label-whitelist=kube_namespace,kube_pod,kube_container
--drop-labels=cmdline,exe
--scrape-timeout=10s
```

sofia: dropping cmdline is good. Also suggest increasing Prometheus scrape interval for this job: 15s -> 30s to reduce churn and CPU

dan: agree on scrape interval bump. Also add metric_relabel_configs in prometheus to filter junk. Example we trialed:

```
metric_relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__name__]
    regex: 'gpu_process_.*'
    action: keep
  - source_labels: [kube_pod]
    regex: '.*test-.*'
    action: drop
  - regex: 'cmdline|exe|container_id'
    action: labeldrop
```

mira: We created a recording rule to avoid storing every pid series, aggregating top processes per GPU instead:

```
- record: gpu:topk_process_gpu_usage:5m
  expr: topk(5, sum by(gpu_id, process_name) (gpu_process_gpu_utilization))
  labels: { aggregation: "topk5" }
```

infra-bot: Deploy: canary=50% started on pool=gpu-nv4, image=rust-gpu-exporter:v0.3.4 — rollstep=serial-10

alex: how will remote_write payloads look? we've had cost spikes when per-node series jump

sofia: rough back-of-envelope: 1000 extra series/node * 200 nodes * 1 sample/15s was scary. With topk + 30s scrape + recording rule we measured ~85% reduction in cardinality & remote_write bytes in our bench runs

jamal: action items from canary:
- apply exporter flags to canary (done)
- change prom scrape interval for gpu-exporter -> 30s (PR open)
- add metric_relabel_configs and recording rule (PR open in observability)
- monitor prometheus_tsdb_head_series, per-node series_count, and remote_write_bytes for 24h

mira: Alert tuning: add `HighExporterSeriesCount` that fires if head_series increases >10% over 1h for scrape_job="gpu-exporter". Use warn then page thresholds so SRE can throttle

```
- alert: HighExporterSeriesCount
  expr: increase(prometheus_tsdb_head_series{job="prometheus-main",scrape_job="gpu-exporter"}[1h]) > 0.1 * avg_over_time(prometheus_tsdb_head_series{job="prometheus-main",scrape_job="gpu-exporter"}[24h])
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: page
```

dan: Also add a Grafana panel: `Top GPU process series` (series_count by node) + sparkline for remote_write_bytes. Make a dashboard row hidden by default to avoid noise for non-SREs

jamal: we'll run the canary for 24h and gate to 100% if series_count + remote_write bytes remain within 10% of baseline. I'll post metric snapshots back here. :thumbsup:

sofia: if noise persists, next step is lightweight eBPF sampling to tag long-running GPU processes and only export those exceeding a usage threshold (e.g., >1% GPU over 30s)

alex: thanks — i'll be on-call for the canary window. ping me if the alert fires
